# Local QA (format, lint, and test)

Run the local QA script `scripts/qa.sh` in this skill.

## Procedure

- Execute the script exactly as shown above when this skill is triggered.
- Capture and summarize key output (success/failure, major warnings, and any files modified).
- If the script fails due to missing tooling (`command not found`, missing executable, or equivalent), install the missing tool(s) and rerun `./scripts/qa.sh`.
- Install tools using this order of preference:
  1. Use the project's package manager when applicable (`uv`/`poetry` for Python, package manager scripts/dependencies for Node.js).
  2. Use a system package manager (`brew` on macOS, `apt` on Debian/Ubuntu) when project-local install is not applicable.
  3. Use language-specific installers as fallback (`pipx`/`pip`, `npm`, `go install`, etc.).
- If multiple tools are missing, repeat install -> rerun until QA completes or you hit a blocker.
- If installation fails or requires unavailable privileges, report what was attempted, the exact failure, and stop.
- Do not run unrelated commands; only run commands needed for QA and missing-tool installation.

# opencode-action

Run an [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) agent from GitHub Actions, including inline pull request review comments, pull request reviews, and manually dispatched tasks.

[![CI](https://github.com/dceoy/opencode-action/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dceoy/opencode-action/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## Quick start

### 1. Add a provider secret

In **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, add the API key for your model provider. The example below uses `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.

### 2. Add the workflow

Create `.github/workflows/opencode.yml`:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode
on:
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  opencode:
    if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '/oc') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/opencode')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run OpenCode
        uses: dceoy/opencode-action@163f9a9cd3d3f497e2847635585419f951371d2f  # v0.8.1
        env:
          OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        with:
          model: opencode-go/kimi-k3
```

### 3. Add an inline comment to a pull request diff

```text
/opencode explain this change
```

The shorter `/oc` trigger also works:

```text
/oc fix this
```

The default setup exchanges the workflow OIDC token for an OpenCode GitHub App token, which requires `id-token: write`.

## Reusable workflows

For smaller caller workflows, this repository provides reusable workflows for OpenCode tasks and pull request reviews:

| Workflow                                                       | Purpose                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`opencode-bot.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-bot.yml)       | Run OpenCode via PR review comments, dispatch, or a fixed prompt.                 |
| [`opencode-review.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml) | Install and use `pr-loop`'s external `pr-review` skill for `pull_request` events. |

See [Reusable workflows](docs/reusable-workflows.md) for caller examples, inputs, secrets, and permission requirements.

## Models and secrets

Set `model` to a `provider/model` value and pass the corresponding API key:

| Provider        | Example model                | Secret               |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------- |
| OpenCode        | `opencode-go/kimi-k3`        | `OPENCODE_API_KEY`   |
| OpenRouter      | `openrouter/openrouter/free` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| Anthropic       | `anthropic/claude-opus-5`    | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`  |
| OpenAI          | `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`         | `OPENAI_API_KEY`     |
| Custom provider | `myprovider/my-model`        | Provider-specific    |

The provider account must have sufficient credits or quota. For providers not built into OpenCode, see [Custom providers](docs/custom-providers.md).

## Sakura AI Engine model synchronization

The optional [Sakura model synchronization workflow](.github/workflows/sync-sakura-models.yml) discovers chat-capable Sakura AI Engine models and opens or updates a pull request when the catalog changes. Configure the `SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY` repository secret before enabling it.

The workflow uses the repository-provided `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; no additional GitHub token secret is required. GitHub does not create new workflow runs for events triggered by `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so pull requests created by this workflow do not automatically trigger `pull_request` workflows. See [GitHub's `GITHUB_TOKEN` documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token).

## Inputs

| Input                 | Default                   | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`               | Required                  | Model in `provider/model` format.                                                                                                                 |
| `agent`               | `build`                   | Primary agent. A slash command can override it.                                                                                                   |
| `prompt`              | Event comment             | Fixed prompt to use instead of the triggering comment.                                                                                            |
| `mentions`            | `/opencode,/oc`           | Comma-separated trigger phrases.                                                                                                                  |
| `variant`             | -                         | Provider-specific reasoning effort; leave empty unless supported. See [Custom providers](docs/custom-providers.md#variants-for-custom-providers). |
| `share`               | `false`                   | Share the OpenCode session.                                                                                                                       |
| `use-github-token`    | `false`                   | Use the workflow token instead of the default App-token flow.                                                                                     |
| `opencode-version`    | Pinned v1                 | OpenCode version to install. The bundled Sakura provider's `chunkTimeout` needs 1.2.25+.                                                          |
| `use-bundled-toolkit` | `true`                    | Install the bundled provider configuration for normal runs or the trusted review bridge for review-only runs.                                     |
| `review-only`         | `false`                   | Enable isolated review execution and install upstream `pr-review`.                                                                                |
| `pr-review-ref`       | Caller-supplied SHA       | Immutable `pr-loop` commit supplying the review skill.                                                                                            |
| `timeout-minutes`     | `60`                      | Stop OpenCode after this many minutes.                                                                                                            |
| `oidc-base-url`       | `https://api.opencode.ai` | OIDC exchange URL for a custom GitHub App installation.                                                                                           |

The default OpenCode binary version is pinned to a stable v1 release and maintained by Renovate (v2 releases are excluded). Set `opencode-version` explicitly to override the default, or use `latest` to opt into runtime resolution.

Direct `workflow_dispatch` uses the same inputs as `workflow_call`; `model` and a non-empty `prompt` are required to run the job.

When `use-github-token: true`, keep `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `env` and grant only the permissions needed for the task.

Outputs are `opencode-version` and `cache-hit`. Review-only runs (`review-only: 'true'`) skip the OpenCode binary cache, install the external `pr-review` skill, and use a disposable temporary HOME (including isolated XDG paths).

## Pull request reviews

The reusable [`opencode-review.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml) runs the SHA-pinned external `pr-loop/pr-review` skill in an isolated `review-only` environment. The old bundled `/review-pr` command, agents, and orchestration are gone. The `/pr-review` prompt loads the skill through OpenCode's native `skill` tool; optional plain-text instructions narrow review focus.

Direct action or bot review-only calls require `use-bundled-toolkit: 'true'`, a full `pr-review-ref` commit SHA, and a concrete PR URL/head SHA. The reusable review workflow retains `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` as public inputs for compatibility; its review agent remains fixed, comment mentions are irrelevant to PR events, and the bundle is required. The action retains its restricted GitHub API adapter and verified App-token publication flow, which are needed to enforce read-only evidence access and a commit-bound `COMMENT` review. The restriction is an OpenCode tool permission boundary, not an operating-system sandbox.

See [Pull request reviews](docs/pull-request-reviews.md) for usage, permissions, trust boundaries, and limitations.

# Pull request reviews

The `opencode-review.yml` reusable workflow restricts reviews to eligible non-draft, non-bot pull requests opened by trusted repository collaborators, independently of the supplied model. It installs the external [`pr-review` skill](https://github.com/dceoy/pr-loop/tree/main/skills/pr-review) from `dceoy/pr-loop`. The bundled `/review-pr` slash command, dedicated agents, scripts, and local skill were removed.

## Invocation

The review workflow uses `review-only: true` and passes the pull request URL and exact head SHA from the event. The public `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` inputs remain available for backward compatibility: the review agent is always restricted to `action-pr-review`, `mentions` has no effect on PR events, and `use-bundled-toolkit: false` is rejected by review-only mode. The action uses `gh skill install dceoy/pr-loop skills/pr-review --pin <SHA> --agent opencode --scope user` to install just the upstream Skill under `~/.config/opencode/skills/pr-review/` at the immutable `pr-review-ref` commit, then invokes it using a plain-text prompt. The workflow loads the installed skill through OpenCode's native `skill` tool; it does not generate a TUI slash command or modify upstream `SKILL.md` metadata. The default `prompt` is `/pr-review`, which is normalized to review focus before that instruction is constructed. Override it with `/pr-review security and performance` or plain-text review focus; the old `/review-pr` command is not supported.

Review-only runs require OpenCode 1.2.14 or newer and GitHub CLI with built-in `gh skill` support (v2.90.0 or newer). The composite action validates the OpenCode version and immutable SHA, then invokes `gh skill` directly in isolated user scope; no custom installer or package manager is needed.

For direct action usage, set `review-only: 'true'`, keep `use-bundled-toolkit: 'true'`, and supply `PR_REVIEW_URL` and `PR_REVIEW_HEAD_SHA` via the environment, or rely on a `pull_request` event. Comment events require both explicit variables. For manual `opencode-bot.yml` runs, provide `pr-review-url` and `pr-review-head-sha`; unresolved targets fail before OpenCode starts. Review requires a model API key and `pull-requests: write`; the default OpenCode App token flow additionally needs `id-token: write`.

```yaml
jobs:
  review:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml@163f9a9cd3d3f497e2847635585419f951371d2f # v0.8.1
    with:
      model: sakura/preview/Kimi-K2.7-Code
      prompt: Focus on security and regression risks.
    secrets:
      SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY }}
```

## GitHub App token reuse

The token resolver (`.opencode/scripts/resolve-app-token.sh`) is preserved independently of the removed review command. The trusted `pr-review-gh.sh` adapter is installed alongside it under `~/.config/opencode/scripts/`. The review prompt instructs the external `pr-review` skill to route GitHub operations through the trusted native API tool and adapter. Review-only runs use the action-defined `action-pr-review` primary agent regardless of the caller's `agent` input. It must run **inside** `opencode github run`: the OpenCode OIDC exchange and Git credential configuration are established at that point, not during action setup.

The adapter extracts token candidates from Git `http.*.extraheader`. Read-only requests never create pending reviews: with `use-github-token: true`, they preserve the caller's workflow credential; otherwise, they use the first candidate when present, or the existing environment credential when no candidate is found. Before publication, the adapter verifies a candidate with a temporary unsubmitted pending-review create/delete probe, then exports the verified credential to its child `gh` process as `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The token is not written to a file or emitted as output.

- **Default (`use-github-token: false`)**: publication requires a verified OpenCode App token; unavailable or mismatched identity fails closed. Read-only requests may use the available scoped credential.
- **Explicit fallback (`use-github-token: true`)**: publication prefers a verified OpenCode App token; otherwise it uses the caller's existing workflow token and its author identity. Read requests preserve that workflow token.

For review-only runs, call the native `pr-review-api` tool with a `request` argument containing a JSON string such as `{ "endpoint": "repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/NUMBER/reviews", "method": "GET", "paginate": true, "page": 1, "offset": 0, "limit": 4096 }`. The trusted tool invokes the adapter through fixed process arguments and stdin; the agent has no shell or file-modification tools. For publication, use `method: "POST"` with an embedded `payload` containing the commit-bound COMMENT review. Unknown fields, duplicate keys, invalid bounds and invalid payloads fail closed. No shell expressions, input paths or CLI flags are accepted.

GET responses contain `offset`, `next_offset`, `page`, `next_page`, `total_chars` and `content`. With `paginate: true`, each request fetches **one** GitHub API page (up to 10 entries); `page` defaults to 1. Reissue the same page at `next_offset` and concatenate `content` until `next_offset` is null. If `next_page` is nonnull, continue with that API page starting at `offset: 0`. A short API page terminates pagination; an exactly full page may require one final empty-page request. This avoids downloading all preceding GitHub API pages for each response slice. Commit `check-runs` and combined `status` endpoints also support pagination; their complete response objects are preserved, with continuation based on the `check_runs` or `statuses` array. Use `paginate: false` for other singleton or immutable endpoints. `offset`/`limit` bound each tool response to at most 4096 characters. Immutable `git/trees/<SHA>` and `git/blobs/<SHA>` endpoints provide frozen file evidence; blobs are decoded as UTF-8, while truncated trees and non-text blobs fail. Mutable API responses can change between slices, so revalidate their snapshot before and after reconstruction. POST accepts no output-paging fields and returns a bounded review receipt; verify the complete persisted review through GET.

The adapter accepts structured requests only through the native `pr-review-api` tool. Direct `gh pr` and `gh api` CLI compatibility, file-based `--input` payloads, and arbitrary CLI formatting flags are not supported. The internal subprocess is independently scoped to the review target and verifies commit-bound `COMMENT` payloads before any write.

Automatic formatters and language servers are disabled in review-only runs.

The adapter resolves credentials for each invocation rather than persisting a short-lived token between processes. Read-only requests use best-effort token resolution; the pending-review probe runs only before publication and performs real GitHub API create/delete operations, although it never publishes a review. The review agent denies tools by default and allows only the upstream skill, trusted reference reads and globbing, and the native API tool. It denies direct GitHub/network tools, general shell commands, grep, delegation, repository edits and all checkout file reads. Repository content is read through frozen Git blobs instead, so checkout symlinks cannot redirect file reads to runner credentials. These are OpenCode tool permissions, **not an operating-system sandbox**; use trusted runners and grant `pull-requests: write`.

## Review contract and boundaries

Upstream `pr-review` freezes the base/head snapshot, validates findings against repository evidence, and publishes one verified `COMMENT` review by default. It never approves, requests changes, merges, or modifies repository contents. See [the upstream skill specification](https://github.com/dceoy/pr-loop/blob/main/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) for the authoritative policy.

Review-only runs use a disposable HOME under the runner's temporary directory, including separate XDG paths, and clean it up at the end. Existing runner OpenCode configuration and binaries are never removed. They disable project configuration and external skill discovery, and use a fresh OpenCode installation. They force the restricted review agent and its tool permissions instead of inheriting the caller's agent permissions. Review behavior remains in the pinned upstream skill; no bundled command or orchestrator is installed.

The upstream skill's default commit SHA is defined by the `pr-review-ref` input in `action.yml`. The reusable review workflow omits this input and inherits the action default automatically. Direct action callers and the bot workflow can still override it; an empty bot-workflow input also falls back to the default in `action.yml`. The post-release CI updates the action default to the latest stable `pr-loop` release SHA via the release-pins PR, without modifying workflow files. `gh skill` installs the specified pinned commit without npm lifecycle scripts or local YAML rewrites. The action checks that the destination is unused, required reference files exist, and the installed Skill contains no symlinks. Failure is terminal; there is no bundled fallback. The existing Bats CI job exercises the exact inline installation command with a real SHA-pinned install. OpenCode GitHub integration can separately add a completion comment.

# Reusable workflows

`opencode-action` publishes two reusable GitHub Actions workflows under `.github/workflows`. Call them as jobs with `uses`, then pass action configuration through `with` and provider credentials through `secrets`.

The examples below pin the reusable workflow definition to a full commit SHA. Inside the called workflow, `uses: $/.` references the action at the repository root from the same repository and running commit, so the workflow reference also pins the action implementation without a second checkout or a separate action revision input.

## Manual dispatch

`opencode-bot.yml` exposes `workflow_dispatch` with the same inputs as `workflow_call`. `model` is required, and `prompt` must be non-empty for the job to run. It can be dispatched from the Actions UI or by API clients and integrations authorized to dispatch GitHub Actions workflows.

## OpenCode bot

Use `opencode-bot.yml` for `/opencode` and `/oc` inline pull request review comments, direct manual dispatch, or another event with a fixed `prompt`.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode
on:
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]

jobs:
  opencode:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-bot.yml@163f9a9cd3d3f497e2847635585419f951371d2f  # v0.8.1
    with:
      model: opencode-go/kimi-k3
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
```

For pull request review comments, the reusable workflow accepts comments only from `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, or `COLLABORATOR` author associations **and** requires a configured `mentions` phrase in the comment body (case-insensitive). Supplying the required `model` input does not bypass either condition. On non-comment events, a non-empty `prompt` is required.

## Pull request review

Use `opencode-review.yml` for automatic reviews on `pull_request` events. It installs the pinned external `pr-loop/pr-review` skill; its default `/pr-review` prompt loads the skill, while plain-text prompts can narrow review focus.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode review
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  review:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml@163f9a9cd3d3f497e2847635585419f951371d2f  # v0.8.1
    with:
      model: openrouter/openrouter/free
    secrets:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
```

This example assumes a trusted, same-repository pull request. For `pull_request` events from public forks, GitHub withholds repository Actions secrets and makes `GITHUB_TOKEN` read-only; Dependabot pull requests have the same restrictions. Private-fork behavior can differ when repository settings explicitly allow secrets or write tokens.

To focus the review, override `prompt` with a supported review aspect, for example `prompt: Focus on security and performance.` See [Pull request reviews](pull-request-reviews.md) for review behavior and security guarantees.

## Inputs

Both reusable workflows expose the action configuration plus a runner input, except that only the bot workflow exposes `pr-review-ref`; the review workflow inherits its default from `action.yml`. The review workflow retains `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` for caller compatibility. Review mode still forces the restricted review agent, ignores comment mentions for PR events, and requires `use-bundled-toolkit: true`:

| Input                 | Default                                                             | Description                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`               | Required                                                            | Model in `provider/model` format.                             |
| `agent`               | `build`                                                             | Primary agent; review-only runs override it.                  |
| `share`               | `false`                                                             | Share the OpenCode session.                                   |
| `prompt`              | `''` for `opencode-bot.yml`; `/pr-review` for `opencode-review.yml` | Fixed prompt.                                                 |
| `use-github-token`    | `false`                                                             | Use the workflow token instead of the default App-token flow. |
| `mentions`            | `/opencode,/oc`                                                     | Comment trigger phrases; unused for PR review events.         |
| `variant`             | `''`                                                                | Provider-specific model variant.                              |
| `oidc-base-url`       | `https://api.opencode.ai`                                           | OIDC exchange base URL.                                       |
| `opencode-version`    | Pinned v1 (see workflow YAML)                                       | OpenCode version to install; Renovate updates the pin.        |
| `use-bundled-toolkit` | `true`                                                              | Review-only mode requires the trusted bundle.                 |
| `review-only`         | `false` on bot; `true` on PR review workflow                        | Install and invoke the upstream review skill.                 |
| `pr-review-ref`       | `action.yml` default (bot only)                                     | Immutable `pr-loop` commit providing the reviewer.            |
| `timeout-minutes`     | `60`                                                                | Maximum OpenCode runtime in minutes.                          |
| `runs-on`             | `ubuntu-latest`                                                     | Runner label for the called job.                              |

The default version is a concrete v1 release pinned in both workflow YAML files and `action.yml`. Renovate updates the pins together while excluding v2 releases. Callers can override `opencode-version`, including using `latest` for runtime resolution.

Direct `workflow_dispatch` on `opencode-bot.yml` uses the same inputs. Its input mappings reference the `workflow_call` definitions via GitHub Actions YAML anchors to avoid drift.

GitHub.com's `$/path` self repository syntax resolves to the repository and commit of the workflow where it appears, including when that workflow is called from another repository. These workflows use `$/.` because the action is defined at the repository root. GitHub Enterprise Server does not support this syntax.

## Secrets

Pass only the provider secret needed by the selected model. The reusable workflows accept `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, and `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`.

`GH_TOKEN` is optional. When omitted, the reusable workflow falls back to the caller's `github.token`. With `use-github-token: true`, that fallback is limited to `contents: read` by the called workflow even if the caller grants `contents: write`. For code-writing operations such as `/oc fix this`, pass a separately write-scoped `GH_TOKEN`; otherwise GitHub API writes to repository contents fail with `403`.

## Permissions

The reusable workflows request `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write`, `id-token: write`, and `actions: read`. A called workflow can only maintain or reduce the caller's `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions: the caller must grant the requested permissions, but its higher `contents` permission cannot override the called workflow's `contents: read` ceiling. A separately supplied `GH_TOKEN` is not governed by that `GITHUB_TOKEN` permission ceiling.

The examples keep `permissions`, `with`, and `secrets` under the calling job so their scopes are explicit: `permissions` controls the caller token, `with` configures the reusable workflow inputs, and `secrets` passes credentials.
